macros.name: bye
macros.doc: \bye is the command to use to terminate a fontinst command file.

macros.name: comment
macros.doc: A comment, which is ignored by fontinst, but typeset as a separate paragraph by fontdoc.

macros.name: declareencoding
macros.doc: This declares which etx file corresponds to which CODINGSCHEME string, and is used when reading metrics in pl format.

macros.name: declarepsencoding
macros.doc: This command specifies how reencoding using a particular etx file should be performed by the driver.

macros.name: declaresize
macros.doc: This declares a new size shorthand, and gives the fd size specifications for it.

macros.name: endreglyphfonts
macros.doc: The effects of modifying reglyphing commands are delimited by \reglyphfonts and \endreglyphfonts, which starts and ends a group respectively.

macros.name: endsetleftboundary
macros.doc: Kerns and ligatures at the left word boundary (beginning of word) are specified using the commands \setleftboundary and \endsetleftboundary, which are syntactically identical to \setslot and \endsetslot respectively.

macros.name: fakenarrow
macros.doc: This command makes \latinfamily fake ‘narrow’ fonts in the family it is working on, by x-scaling the normal fonts.

macros.name: fontinstcc
macros.doc: \fontinstcc switches to the catcodes used in e.g. fontinst.sty: _ and @ are letters, space and newline are ignored, and ~ is a space.

macros.name: fromafm
macros.doc: \fromafm, \frompl, and \fromplgivenetx write out an mtx file corresponding to the afm or pl file.

macros.name: fromany
macros.doc: \fromany looks for a file in any of the formats (in the order mtx, pl, afm) and behaves as the first \from. . . for which it found a file.

macros.name: frompl
macros.doc: \fromafm, \frompl, and \fromplgivenetx write out an mtx file corresponding to the afm or pl file.

macros.name: fromplgivenetx
macros.doc: \fromplgivenetx permits specifying which encoding file to use when associating glyph names to slots, whereas \frompl tries to guess this from the CODINGSCHEME property of the pl file.

macros.name: glyph
macros.doc: Sets the named glyph ⟨glyph⟩ at the given scale, with 1000 as the natural size.

macros.name: ifdirect
macros.doc: The \ifdirect conditional can be used to disambiguate the inverse mapping, by conditionalising all undesired \setslots on that the file is being interpreted in the direct mode.

macros.name: ifisinslot
macros.doc: During vpl /pl generation, this conditional tests whether glyph ⟨glyph⟩ (a string expression) is put in the slot ⟨slot⟩ (an integer expression).

macros.name: ifoption
macros.doc: Test whether ⟨string⟩ (a string expression) is among the current list of options.

macros.name: installfamily
macros.doc: This tells fontinst to write an fd file for the given combination of encoding and family, and clears the internal list of entries to put in that file.

macros.name: installfontas
macros.doc: The \installfontas command does not itself create the font, it just makes a note that the specified font declaration should be written to the proper FD file at \endinstallfonts.

macros.name: installfonts
macros.doc: At \installfonts, fontinst’s internal list of fd files to generate are cleared.

macros.name: int
macros.doc: Returns the value of the integer variable ⟨int⟩.

macros.name: italic
macros.doc: Returns the width, height, depth, or italic correction of the glyph variable ⟨glyph⟩.

macros.name: kerning
macros.doc: Returns the kerning between the ⟨left⟩ and ⟨right⟩ glyphs.

macros.name: label
macros.doc: A reference label (like in LaTeX), which records the slot number and glyph name.

macros.name: latinfamily
macros.doc: This command is by itself an entire \installfonts . . . \endinstallfonts block, automatically doing \transformfonts, \installfonts, and \installrawfonts depending on which base font metrics it finds.

macros.name: Ligature
macros.doc: The \Ligature command is by default a synonym of \ligature (but fontdoc may typeset them differently).

macros.name: makerightboundary
macros.doc: This makes the current slot the end of word (right boundary) marker with respect to ligatures and kerning, i.e., TeX will kern and ligature as if there was an invisible occurrence of this character after the last character of every word.

macros.name: messagebreak
macros.doc: Used to start a new line in an ⟨error⟩, ⟨help⟩, ⟨warning⟩, or ⟨info⟩ message.

macros.name: moveup
macros.doc: Moves up by the given amount, and advances the current vertical offset.

macros.name: needsfontinstversion
macros.doc: This issues a warning if the current version of the fontinst package is less than ⟨version⟩.

macros.name: needsTeXextension
macros.doc: The \needsTeXextension command issues a warning if fontinst is not being run on one of the listed extensions of TeX.

macros.name: nextlarger
macros.doc: makes ⟨glyph⟩ the NEXTLARGER entry of the current slot.

macros.name: nextslot
macros.doc: Sets the number of the next slot.

macros.name: NOFILES
macros.doc: This command switches off file generation, and causes fontinst to only generate empty files.

macros.name: normalcc
macros.doc: \normalcc switches back to normal catcodes.

macros.name: offcommand
macros.doc: \offcommand turns off a command, i.e., it redefines it to do nothing (while still taking the same number of arguments).

macros.name: offmtxcommand
macros.doc: Turning a command ‘off’ using \offmtxcommand means no such commands are to be copied to a destination font by \reglyphfont.

macros.name: oncommand
macros.doc: \oncommand turns a command back on, i.e., it restores the definition the command had before a previous \offcommand.

macros.name: reglyphfonts
macros.doc: The effects of modifying reglyphing commands are delimited by \reglyphfonts and \endreglyphfonts, which starts and ends a group respectively.

macros.name: renameglyph
macros.doc: \renameglyph simply declares that occurrences of the glyph name ⟨from⟩ should be replaced by the glyph name ⟨to⟩.

macros.name: renameglyphweighted
macros.doc: The \renameglyph and \renameglyphweighted commands cause each reference to the glyph ⟨from⟩ in the source font to be replaced by a reference to the glyph ⟨to⟩ in the destination font.

macros.name: resetkern
macros.doc: \resetkern unconditionally sets a kern between the two glyphs, scaled by the current value of rawscale.

macros.name: samesize
macros.doc: Sets the dimensions of the current glyph to be the same as ⟨glyph⟩.

macros.name: setint
macros.doc: If the integer variable ⟨int⟩ is currently undefined, it is defined to be the current value of hinteger expressioni.

macros.name: setkern
macros.doc: This sets a kern between the two glyphs, scaled by the current value of rawscale, unless such a kern already has been set.

macros.name: setleftboundary
macros.doc: Kerns and ligatures at the left word boundary (beginning of word) are specified using the commands \setleftboundary and \endsetleftboundary, which are syntactically identical to \setslot and \endsetslot respectively.

macros.name: setrightboundary
macros.doc: Makes the end of a word (right boundary) behave like the left side of ⟨glyph⟩ with respect to kerning and ligatures.

macros.name: SlantAmount
macros.doc: Slant factor used for faking oblique shape.

macros.name: slanteditalcorr
macros.doc: The integer expression used to calculate a guess for the italic correction of glyphs in a font with positive slant.

macros.name: slotexample
macros.doc: This typesets the character in the current slot from the example font (cf. \useexamplefont).

macros.name: substitutenoisy
macros.doc: \substitutenoisy means that a warning will be given when the substitution is made by LaTeX.

macros.name: substitutesilent
macros.doc: \substitutesilent means that LaTeX should not warn when the font substitution is made.

macros.name: transformfont
macros.doc: This makes a raw transformed font, for example expanded, slanted, condensed or re-encoded.

macros.name: unsetglyph
macros.doc: Makes the glyph called ⟨name⟩ undefined.

macros.name: unsetstr
macros.doc: The \unsetstr command unconditionally renders the string variable ⟨name⟩ unset.

macros.name: uprightitalcorr
macros.doc: The integer expression used to calculate a guess for the italic correction of glyphs in a font with non-positive slant.
